chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when (2E,4Z,6E)-Octatriene is treated with Heat (thermal, disrotatory)?
questions.explanation: Treating (2E,4Z,6E)-Octatriene with Heat (thermal, disrotatory) yields cis-5,6-Dimethyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene. Rationale: Ground-state HOMO (psi 4) undergoes disrotatory ring closure to bring methyl groups into cis-geometry.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of (2E,4Z,6E)-Octatriene into trans-5,6-Dimethyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene?
questions.explanation: To convert (2E,4Z,6E)-Octatriene into trans-5,6-Dimethyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene, the appropriate reagent is Light (hν, photochemical, conrotatory). Rationale: Excited-state HOMO (psi 5*) undergoes conrotatory ring closure to rotate methyl groups into trans-geometry.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when (2E,4E)-Hexadiene is treated with Heat (thermal, conrotatory)?
questions.explanation: Treating (2E,4E)-Hexadiene with Heat (thermal, conrotatory) yields trans-3,4-Dimethylcyclobutene. Rationale: Ground-state HOMO (psi 2) undergoes conrotatory lobe rotation, placing methyl groups trans to one another.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of (2E,4E)-Hexadiene into cis-3,4-Dimethylcyclobutene?
questions.explanation: To convert (2E,4E)-Hexadiene into cis-3,4-Dimethylcyclobutene, the appropriate reagent is Light (hν, photochemical, disrotatory). Rationale: Excited-state HOMO (psi 3*) undergoes disrotatory lobe rotation, yielding the cis-cyclobutene isomer.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1,3-Butadiene + Ethylene is treated with Heat (thermal suprafacial-suprafacial)?
questions.explanation: Treating 1,3-Butadiene + Ethylene with Heat (thermal suprafacial-suprafacial) yields Cyclohexene. Rationale: HOMO of diene (psi 2) and LUMO of dienophile (pi*) match orbital symmetry in a concerted suprafacial manner.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2 equivalents Ethylene into Cyclobutane?
questions.explanation: To convert 2 equivalents Ethylene into Cyclobutane, the appropriate reagent is Light (hν, 300 nm). Rationale: Photoexcitation promotes an electron into pi*, allowing symmetry-allowed concerted [2+2] cycloaddition.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Heat (300°C) to yield 2,6-Octadiene as the major product?
questions.explanation: 3,4-Dimethyl-1,5-hexadiene reacts with Heat (300°C) to yield 2,6-Octadiene. Rationale: Concerted [3,3]-sigmatropic migration of a C-C sigma bond through a 6-membered chair-like transition state.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Allyl phenyl ether is treated with Heat (200°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Allyl phenyl ether with Heat (200°C) yields 2-Allylphenol. Rationale: Thermal [3,3]-sigmatropic shift forms a cyclohexadienone intermediate that rapidly enolizes to 2-allylphenol.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Heat (100°C) to yield 4-Pentenal as the major product?
questions.explanation: Allyl vinyl ether reacts with Heat (100°C) to yield 4-Pentenal. Rationale: Concerted [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of allyl vinyl ether yields an unconjugated gamma,delta-unsaturated aldehyde.

questions.chapter_title: Orbitals and Organic Chemistry: Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when (3Z)-1,3-Pentadiene-5-d is treated with Heat (200°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating (3Z)-1,3-Pentadiene-5-d with Heat (200°C) yields (1E)-1,3-Pentadiene-1-d. Rationale: Concerted suprafacial transfer of hydrogen across the 5-carbon conjugated pi system.
